text:
Predicates:
Cute(x) ::: x is cute.
SpotNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Rockie ::: Rockie.
Premises:
∀x (SpotNearCampus(x) ∧ Rabbit(x) → Cute(x)) ::: All rabbits that can be spotted near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ SpotNearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x (SpotNearCampus(x) ∧ (Rabbit(x) ∨ Squirrel(x)) → SpotNearCampus(x)) ::: The only animals that can be spotted near the campus are rabbits and squirrels.
∀x (SpotNearCampus(x) ∧ Squirrel(x) → Skittish(x)) ::: All the squirrels that can be spotted near the campus are skittish.
SpotNearCampus(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus.
¬Calm(Rockie) ::: Rockie is not calm.
Conclusion:
(Cute(Rockie) ∧ Calm(Rockie)) → (Skittish(Rockie) ∧ Turtle(Rockie)) ::: If Rockie is cute and calm, then Rockie is a skittish turtle.
